source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Types of Transformer: Auto Transformer (saving of copper -rating of autotransformers)
stem: The saving of copper in an autotransformer compared with an equivalent two-winding transformer is:
options: \((1-1/a)\) times, where a is the transformation ratio
explanation: Autotransformers are most economical when the ratio is close to unity, as part of the winding is common.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Types of Transformer: Auto Transformer (saving of copper -rating of autotransformers)
stem: A major disadvantage of an autotransformer is:
options: The absence of electrical isolation between primary and secondary
explanation: A direct electrical connection makes an HV fault dangerous on the LV side, so isolation transformers are used instead.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Parallel operation and load sharing
stem: For satisfactory parallel operation of two single-phase transformers, it is essential that they have:
options: The same voltage ratio and the same polarity
explanation: Unequal ratios cause circulating current; equal per-unit impedance ensures load sharing in proportion to rating.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Tertiary winding
stem: A tertiary (delta) winding is provided in a three-phase star-star transformer mainly to:
options: Provide a path for third harmonic currents and stabilise the neutral
explanation: Circulating triplen harmonics in the closed delta keep the flux and phase voltages nearly sinusoidal.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Electromechanical energy conversion Principle: Field energy and co-energy
stem: In a singly excited magnetic system with a linear magnetic circuit, the field energy and co-energy are:
explanation: For a linear λ-i characteristic both equal ½Li²; they differ only when saturation makes the curve non-linear.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Torque and force in singly excited and multiple excited electromechanical systems and applications
stem: The mechanical force developed in a singly excited electromagnetic system is obtained as:
options: The integral of flux over time
The partial derivative of co-energy with respect to displacement at constant current
The product of flux and current
explanation: F = ∂W′/∂x at constant i, or equivalently −∂W/∂x at constant flux linkage.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Armature windings simplex lap and wave windings
stem: In a simplex lap winding, the number of parallel paths equals:
explanation: Lap winding gives A = P and suits low-voltage high-current machines; wave winding always gives A = 2.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Armature windings simplex lap and wave windings
stem: A simplex wave winding is preferred for machines requiring:
explanation: With only two parallel paths, more conductors are in series, giving a higher generated voltage.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Induced EMF: EMF equations- electromagnetic torque- numerical problems
stem: The e.m.f. generated in a DC machine is:
explanation: Z is total armature conductors, P poles, A parallel paths and N the speed in r.p.m.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Induced EMF: EMF equations- electromagnetic torque- numerical problems
stem: A 6-pole wave-wound DC generator has 600 conductors, flux 25 mWb per pole and runs at 500 r.p.m. The generated e.m.f. is:
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Derivation of the back EMF equation and torque equation
stem: The torque developed by a DC motor is proportional to:
explanation: T = (PZ/2πA)φIa, so torque is the product of flux and armature current.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Armature Reaction
stem: Armature reaction in a DC machine is the effect of:
options: The armature MMF distorting and weakening the main field flux
The field winding on the armature
explanation: It produces cross-magnetising and, with a shifted brush axis, demagnetising components.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Compensating winding
stem: Compensating windings in a DC machine are placed in the pole faces to:
options: Improve commutation only at the brushes
Neutralise the cross-magnetising armature reaction under the pole arc
explanation: They carry armature current in the opposite sense, preventing flashover in machines with rapidly changing loads.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Interpoles- numerical problems
stem: Interpoles (commutating poles) in a DC machine are provided mainly to:
options: Neutralise reactance voltage and improve commutation
explanation: They are connected in series with the armature so that their flux tracks the load current.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Voltage build-up in a DC Generator
stem: A DC shunt generator fails to build up voltage if:
options: There is no residual magnetism or the field resistance exceeds the critical value
explanation: Build-up needs residual flux, correct field connection polarity and field resistance below the critical value.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Critical field resistance
stem: The critical field resistance of a DC shunt generator is:
options: The slope of the tangent to the initial part of the open-circuit characteristic
explanation: If the field circuit resistance exceeds this value, the resistance line misses the OCC and no build-up occurs.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Commutation
stem: The commutator of a DC generator converts the alternating e.m.f. induced in the armature into a unidirectional output.
explanation: It acts as a mechanical rectifier by reversing connections as each coil passes the magnetic neutral axis.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Determination of its parameters from O.C and S.C tests
stem: The iron loss of a transformer is practically independent of the load current.
explanation: Core loss depends on flux, which is fixed by the applied voltage and frequency, not by the load.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Interpoles- numerical problems
stem:
Assertion (A): Interpoles are connected in series with the armature.
Reason (R): The reactance voltage to be neutralised is proportional to the armature current, so the interpole flux must vary with it.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Series connection makes the compensating flux automatically track the load, exactly as R states.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Efficiency
stem:
Assertion (A): A transformer has higher efficiency than a rotating machine of the same rating.
Reason (R): Being static, it has no friction and windage losses.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Absence of mechanical losses lets large transformers reach 98–99% efficiency, so R explains A.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Armature windings simplex lap and wave windings
stem: Which statements about DC machine armature windings are correct? (Select all that apply)
options: Simplex lap winding has A = P parallel paths
Simplex wave winding has A = 2 parallel paths
Lap winding is preferred for high-current low-voltage machines
explanation: Equalizer rings are needed for lap windings, where unequal path e.m.f.s would otherwise circulate current.
source: BEU syllabus — Electrical Machine-I, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: The fundamental difference between a microprocessor and a microcontroller is that a microcontroller:
options: Integrates CPU, memory and I/O peripherals on a single chip
explanation: A microprocessor needs external memory and I/O; a microcontroller is a self-contained system.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: In Von Neumann architecture, program and data:
options: Share the same memory space and bus
explanation: Harvard architecture uses separate program and data memories, allowing simultaneous access.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: The 8051 microcontroller follows which architecture?
explanation: Separate program (ROM) and data (RAM) address spaces allow overlapping fetch and execute.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: The program counter of a microprocessor holds:
options: The address of the next instruction to be fetched
explanation: It increments automatically after each fetch unless a branch modifies it.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: The address bus of a microprocessor is:
options: Unidirectional, from the CPU to memory/IO
explanation: The data bus is bidirectional; the address bus is driven only by the CPU.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: A processor with a 16-bit address bus can directly address:
explanation: 2^16 = 65536 distinct locations.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: The instruction cycle of a microprocessor consists of:
explanation: Some instructions add memory read/write machine cycles to the execute phase.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: A RISC processor is characterised by:
options: A small set of simple fixed-length instructions executed in few cycles
explanation: CISC uses complex instructions; RISC relies on many registers and pipelining.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: Pipelining in a processor improves performance by:
options: Overlapping the fetch, decode and execute stages of successive instructions
explanation: Throughput approaches one instruction per cycle despite multi-cycle latency.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: A stack in a microprocessor operates on the principle of:
explanation: It is used for subroutine return addresses and register saving during interrupts.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit microcontrollers and comparison
stem: An 8-bit microcontroller means its:
options: ALU and internal data bus handle 8 bits at a time
explanation: The data word width defines the classification, not the address bus width.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit microcontrollers and comparison
stem: The 8051 has an internal RAM of:
explanation: The standard 8051 has 128 bytes of on-chip data RAM plus the special function registers.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit microcontrollers and comparison
stem: The 8051 has on-chip program memory of:
explanation: It can be externally expanded up to 64 KB of program memory.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit microcontrollers and comparison
stem: The maximum external data memory addressable by the 8051 is:
explanation: The 16-bit DPTR register addresses up to 64 KB of external RAM.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit microcontrollers and comparison
stem: Compared with an 8-bit microcontroller, a 32-bit microcontroller offers:
options: Wider data handling, more memory and higher processing throughput
explanation: ARM Cortex-M devices are typical 32-bit microcontrollers used in modern embedded designs.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit microcontrollers and comparison
stem: The AVR and PIC families differ from the 8051 mainly in that they:
options: Use RISC-style instruction sets with more single-cycle instructions
explanation: Modern 8-bit RISC cores execute most instructions in one clock cycle.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit microcontrollers and comparison
stem: A 16-bit microcontroller such as the MSP430 is often chosen for:
explanation: Its low active and sleep currents suit portable instrumentation.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit microcontrollers and comparison
stem: MIPS as a performance measure for microcontrollers stands for:
explanation: It depends on both clock frequency and the cycles per instruction.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: An embedded system is best defined as:
options: A computing system dedicated to a specific function within a larger product
explanation: It is application-specific with tight constraints on cost, power and size.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: A key characteristic of most embedded systems is:
options: General-purpose programmability by the end user
explanation: Deadlines, low power and limited memory dominate embedded design decisions.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: A hard real-time system is one in which:
options: Missing a deadline constitutes total system failure
explanation: Airbag controllers and flight control systems are classic hard real-time examples.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: Firmware in an embedded system refers to:
options: Software stored permanently in non-volatile memory on the device
explanation: It is typically held in flash or ROM and rarely changed after deployment.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: A watchdog timer in a microcontroller is used to:
options: Reset the system if the software fails to service it within a set time
explanation: It recovers the system from software hangs or lock-ups automatically.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: The 8051 has how many 8-bit I/O ports?
explanation: 32 I/O lines in total, some of which are multiplexed with other functions.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: The 8051 contains how many 16-bit timers/counters?
explanation: The 8052 variant adds a third timer, Timer 2.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: The 8051 supports how many interrupt sources in its basic version?
explanation: Two external, two timer and one serial port interrupt source.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: The 8051 provides a full-duplex serial port of type:
explanation: Its baud rate is usually generated by Timer 1 in auto-reload mode.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: One machine cycle of a standard 8051 consists of:
explanation: At 12 MHz, one machine cycle takes 1 microsecond.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: With a 12 MHz crystal, an 8051 instruction taking two machine cycles executes in:
explanation: Each machine cycle is 12/12 MHz = 1 us, so two cycles take 2 us.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: The 8051 family member 8052 differs from the 8051 in having:
options: 8 KB ROM, 256 bytes RAM and a third timer
explanation: It is upward compatible, retaining the same core instruction set.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: The 8031 differs from the 8051 in that it:
options: Has no on-chip ROM and must use external program memory
explanation: Its EA pin must be tied low to force all fetches to external memory.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: A real-time operating system (RTOS) is used in an embedded system to:
options: Schedule multiple tasks with deterministic timing guarantees
explanation: Priority-based preemptive scheduling ensures critical tasks meet their deadlines.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: The control bus of a microprocessor carries signals such as:
options: RD, WR, ALE and interrupt acknowledgements
explanation: Control signals coordinate the timing and direction of bus transactions.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem: A microcontroller is generally better suited than a microprocessor for a dedicated control application.
explanation: On-chip memory, timers and I/O reduce the component count, cost and board size.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: The 8051 uses the same address space for program and data memory.
explanation: Its Harvard architecture provides separate 64 KB program and data address spaces.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Microprocessor architecture fundamentals
stem:
Assertion (A): Harvard architecture can be faster than Von Neumann architecture.
Reason (R): Separate program and data buses allow an instruction fetch and a data access simultaneously.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Eliminating the single-bus bottleneck permits overlapped fetch and execute operations.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem:
Assertion (A): A watchdog timer improves the reliability of an embedded system.
Reason (R): It periodically increases the processor clock frequency.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: The watchdog resets the system on software failure; it does not alter the clock frequency.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: Embedded systems and the 8051 family overview
stem: Which features are integrated on a standard 8051 chip?
explanation: The classic 8051 has no ADC; that is added only in enhanced derivatives.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 1

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The 8086 microprocessor has a data bus and address bus of:
explanation: The 20-bit address bus allows 1 MB of physical memory to be addressed.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The 8086 can address a maximum physical memory of:
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The 8086 architecture is divided into:
options: Bus Interface Unit (BIU) and Execution Unit (EU)
explanation: The BIU fetches instructions into a queue while the EU executes, giving pipelining.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The instruction queue of the 8086 is:
explanation: The 8088 has a 4-byte queue; prefetching hides memory access latency.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The physical address in the 8086 is computed as:
explanation: The segment value is shifted left by four bits before adding the 16-bit offset.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: If CS = 2000H and IP = 0100H, the physical address of the next instruction is:
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The four segment registers of the 8086 are:
explanation: Code, data, stack and extra segments, each defining a 64 KB window.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The maximum size of one 8086 segment is:
explanation: The 16-bit offset limits each segment to 65536 bytes.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The 8086 flag register contains how many conditional (status) flags?
explanation: Carry, parity, auxiliary carry, zero, sign and overflow, plus three control flags.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The ALE signal of the 8086 is used to:
options: Latch the lower address bits from the multiplexed AD0-AD15 bus
explanation: An external 8282/74LS373 latch captures the address during T1.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The 8086 operates in minimum mode when the MN/MX pin is:
explanation: In maximum mode (MN/MX low), an 8288 bus controller generates the control signals.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: Maximum mode of the 8086 is used when the system:
options: Includes a coprocessor such as the 8087 or multiple bus masters
explanation: Status lines S0-S2 drive the 8288 to generate the extended control signals.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The BHE (Bus High Enable) signal of the 8086 indicates:
options: A transfer on the upper byte of the data bus (D8-D15)
explanation: BHE with A0 selects byte or word accesses in the odd/even memory banks.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: The instruction MOV AX, 1234H uses which addressing mode?
explanation: The operand is a constant contained in the instruction itself.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: MOV AX, BX is an example of:
explanation: Both source and destination are CPU registers, so no memory access occurs.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: MOV AX, [BX] is an example of:
explanation: BX holds the offset of the operand within the data segment.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: MOV AX, [BX + SI + 10H] uses which addressing mode?
explanation: Base register plus index register plus displacement forms the effective address.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: The default segment register used with SP and BP is:
explanation: BX, SI and DI default to DS, while BP and SP default to SS.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: The XCHG instruction in 8086:
options: Exchanges the contents of two operands
explanation: At least one operand must be a register; memory-to-memory is not allowed.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: The CMP instruction affects the flags by:
options: Subtracting the source from the destination without storing the result
Storing the difference in the destination
explanation: It is normally followed by a conditional jump such as JE, JG or JB.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: The LOOP instruction in 8086 uses which register as the counter?
explanation: CX is decremented and the jump is taken while it remains non-zero.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: After a MUL instruction with an 8-bit operand, the 16-bit product is stored in:
explanation: A 16-bit multiply gives a 32-bit result in DX:AX.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: The DIV instruction with a 16-bit divisor leaves the quotient and remainder in:
explanation: The 32-bit dividend is taken from DX:AX before the operation.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: String instructions such as MOVSB use which register pair by default?
options: DS:SI as source and ES:DI as destination
explanation: The direction flag determines whether SI and DI increment or decrement.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: The REP prefix used with string instructions repeats the operation until:
explanation: REPE and REPNE additionally test the zero flag for comparison strings.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: The instruction that translates a byte using a lookup table pointed to by BX is:
explanation: AL is used as the index and is replaced by the table entry at DS:BX+AL.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: The LEA instruction is used to:
options: Load the data at an address
Load the effective address (offset) of a memory operand into a register
explanation: It computes the offset without performing a memory read.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Assembler directives, procedures and macros
stem: Assembler directives such as DB, DW and DD are:
options: Pseudo-instructions that guide the assembler but generate no machine code themselves
explanation: They reserve and initialise storage or control assembly, not runtime behaviour.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Assembler directives, procedures and macros
stem: The directive DW reserves storage of:
explanation: DB is one byte, DW two, DD four and DQ eight.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Assembler directives, procedures and macros
stem: The ASSUME directive in 8086 assembly is used to:
options: Tell the assembler which segment register corresponds to each segment
explanation: It lets the assembler compute correct segment overrides at assembly time.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Assembler directives, procedures and macros
stem: A NEAR procedure call differs from a FAR call in that NEAR:
options: Pushes only IP, since the procedure is in the same code segment
explanation: A FAR call pushes both CS and IP and is matched by a far RET.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Assembler directives, procedures and macros
stem: The main difference between a macro and a procedure is that a macro:
options: Is expanded inline at each invocation, increasing code size but avoiding call overhead
explanation: A procedure exists once in memory and is reached by CALL/RET.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Assembler directives, procedures and macros
stem: Parameters can be passed to an 8086 procedure using:
options: Registers, the stack or a memory block
explanation: Stack passing supports recursion and re-entrancy, unlike fixed memory locations.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Assembler directives, procedures and macros
stem: The INT 21H instruction in an 8086 program invokes:
options: A DOS function call service routine
explanation: The function number is placed in AH before the software interrupt is issued.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: The 8086 BIU and EU can operate concurrently.
explanation: Instruction prefetching by the BIU overlaps with execution by the EU, giving basic pipelining.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Addressing modes and instruction set of 8086
stem: Memory-to-memory data transfer is permitted by the 8086 MOV instruction.
explanation: At least one operand must be a register; only string instructions move memory to memory.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem:
Assertion (A): The 8086 uses a segmented memory architecture.
Reason (R): It has a 20-bit address bus but only 16-bit internal registers.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Segmentation combines a shifted 16-bit segment with a 16-bit offset to form a 20-bit address.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: Assembler directives, procedures and macros
stem:
Assertion (A): Macros execute faster than procedures.
Reason (R): Macro code is inserted inline, avoiding call and return overhead.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: No stack operations or branches are needed, at the cost of larger overall program size.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8086 architecture and pin diagram
stem: Which registers are part of the 8086 Bus Interface Unit?
explanation: The ALU, general registers and flags belong to the Execution Unit.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 2

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The accumulator of the 8051 is designated as:
options: A (or ACC), an 8-bit special function register
explanation: Most arithmetic and logic operations involve the accumulator.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The 8051 has how many register banks of eight registers each?
explanation: Banks occupy internal RAM 00H-1FH and are selected by RS1 and RS0 in the PSW.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The register bank is selected in the 8051 using bits:
options: RS1 and RS0 of the PSW
explanation: Bank 0 is the default after reset, occupying addresses 00H to 07H.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The stack pointer of the 8051 is:
explanation: It is usually relocated above the register banks and bit-addressable area.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The 8051 stack grows:
options: Upward, with SP incremented before a PUSH
explanation: This differs from many processors where the stack grows toward lower addresses.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The bit-addressable RAM area of the 8051 occupies internal addresses:
explanation: These 16 bytes provide bit addresses 00H to 7FH for single-bit operations.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The special function registers of the 8051 occupy internal addresses:
explanation: Only some SFR addresses are implemented, and those ending in 0H or 8H are bit-addressable.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The DPTR of the 8051 is a 16-bit register formed by:
explanation: It is used to address external data memory and program lookup tables.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: Port 0 of the 8051 requires external pull-up resistors because:
options: It has open-drain outputs without internal pull-ups
explanation: Ports 1, 2 and 3 have internal pull-ups; Port 0 does not when used as general I/O.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: When external memory is used, Port 0 and Port 2 of the 8051 serve as:
options: The multiplexed low address/data bus and the high address bus respectively
explanation: ALE demultiplexes the low byte of the address from Port 0.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The alternate functions of Port 3 pins include:
options: RXD, TXD, INT0, INT1, T0, T1, WR and RD
explanation: Each P3 bit has a dedicated peripheral function when enabled.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: After a reset, the program counter of the 8051 contains:
explanation: Execution always begins at address 0000H of the program memory.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The interrupt vector address of external interrupt INT0 in the 8051 is:
explanation: Timer 0 is 000BH, INT1 is 0013H, Timer 1 is 001BH and serial is 0023H.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The EA pin of the 8051 must be tied low when:
options: All program code resides in external memory
explanation: EA high makes the CPU fetch from internal ROM up to the on-chip limit.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: The instruction MOV A, #55H uses which addressing mode?
explanation: The hash symbol indicates an immediate constant operand.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: The instruction MOV A, R3 uses:
explanation: The operand is one of the eight registers in the active bank.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: The instruction MOV A, @R0 uses:
options: Register indirect addressing of internal RAM
explanation: Only R0 and R1 can serve as pointers for indirect internal RAM access.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: The instruction MOVC A, @A+DPTR uses:
options: Indexed addressing to read a program memory lookup table
explanation: MOVC accesses code memory, useful for storing constant tables in ROM.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: To read a byte from external data memory the 8051 uses:
explanation: MOVX asserts RD and accesses the external RAM address space.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: The instruction SETB P1.0 is an example of:
explanation: The 8051 has a rich set of single-bit boolean instructions.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: The instruction DJNZ R2, LOOP performs:
options: Decrement R2 and jump to LOOP if the result is not zero
explanation: It is the standard way of building counted loops and delay routines.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: The SJMP instruction of the 8051 uses:
options: Relative addressing with a range of -128 to +127 bytes
explanation: LJMP provides a full 64 KB range and AJMP an 11-bit page range.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: The CJNE instruction affects which flag?
options: The carry flag, set if the destination is less than the source
explanation: This allows greater-than and less-than tests after the compare.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: The DA A instruction is used after:
options: Adding two packed BCD numbers, to correct the result
explanation: It adjusts the accumulator by adding 6 to nibbles that exceed 9.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: MUL AB in the 8051 stores the 16-bit product in:
explanation: The OV flag is set if the product exceeds 255.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: The instruction that copies the carry flag into a bit location is:
explanation: The carry acts as the boolean accumulator for bit operations.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 memory and I/O interfacing with peripherals
stem: The 8051 signal used to demultiplex the address and data on Port 0 is:
explanation: An external latch captures the low address byte on the falling edge of ALE.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 memory and I/O interfacing with peripherals
stem: The PSEN signal of the 8051 is activated when:
explanation: External data memory reads use RD instead, keeping the two spaces separate.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 memory and I/O interfacing with peripherals
stem: An ADC0808 interfaced to the 8051 needs which control signals from the microcontroller?
options: SOC (start of conversion) and channel select, with EOC read back
explanation: The EOC line can be polled or connected to an external interrupt pin.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 memory and I/O interfacing with peripherals
stem: A DAC0808 interfaced to an 8051 port converts:
options: An 8-bit digital value into a proportional analog current
explanation: An op-amp current-to-voltage converter usually follows the DAC output.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 memory and I/O interfacing with peripherals
stem: Timer 0 of the 8051 in mode 1 operates as:
explanation: Mode 0 is 13-bit, mode 2 is 8-bit auto-reload and mode 3 splits Timer 0.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 memory and I/O interfacing with peripherals
stem: Timer mode 2 of the 8051 is commonly used for:
options: Serial port baud rate generation, due to its auto-reload feature
explanation: TH1 reloads TL1 automatically, giving a stable periodic overflow rate.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 memory and I/O interfacing with peripherals
stem: A matrix keyboard is interfaced to the 8051 using:
options: Row scanning with column reading and software debouncing
explanation: A 4x4 matrix needs only 8 I/O lines for 16 keys.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 memory and I/O interfacing with peripherals
stem: Multiplexed seven-segment displays are driven by the 8051 by:
options: Sending segment data and enabling one digit at a time rapidly
explanation: Persistence of vision makes rapidly scanned digits appear continuously lit.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: The 8051 stack can be located in external RAM.
explanation: The 8-bit stack pointer restricts the stack to the internal 256-byte RAM space.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 addressing modes and instruction set
stem: The 8051 has instructions that operate on single bits.
explanation: Its boolean processor supports SETB, CLR, CPL, JB, JNB and similar bit operations.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 memory and I/O interfacing with peripherals
stem:
Assertion (A): The ALE signal is essential when the 8051 uses external memory.
Reason (R): Port 0 carries both the low address byte and the data byte in a time-multiplexed manner.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: ALE strobes an external latch to hold the address while Port 0 switches to data.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem:
Assertion (A): Port 0 needs external pull-up resistors for general purpose output.
Reason (R): Port 0 pins have open-drain drivers with no internal pull-up transistors.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Without pull-ups the port cannot source a logic high level.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: 8051 internal architecture, registers, SFRs and memory
stem: Which of the following are special function registers of the 8051?
explanation: R7 is a general-purpose bank register in internal RAM, not an SFR.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 3

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: In asynchronous serial communication, synchronisation between transmitter and receiver is achieved using:
options: Start and stop bits framing each character
explanation: Both ends must be preset to the same baud rate; no clock is transmitted.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: Synchronous serial communication differs from asynchronous in that it:
options: Transmits a clock signal or embeds clocking, giving higher throughput
explanation: Removing per-character framing overhead improves efficiency for block transfers.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: Baud rate is defined as:
options: The number of bytes per second
The number of signalling symbol changes per second
explanation: For simple binary signalling, baud rate equals bit rate.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: A serial link at 9600 baud with 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit transmits how many characters per second?
explanation: Each character needs 10 bit times, so 9600/10 = 960 characters per second.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: The RS232 standard defines a logic 1 (mark) as:
options: A negative voltage, typically -3 V to -15 V
explanation: Logic 0 (space) is positive; the inverted bipolar levels improve noise immunity.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: A MAX232 IC is used in a microcontroller system to:
options: Convert TTL logic levels to RS232 voltage levels and back
explanation: Internal charge pumps generate the required +/-10 V from a single 5 V supply.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: RS232 is characterised as:
options: A single-ended, point-to-point interface limited to about 15 m
explanation: RS485 uses differential signalling for long distance multi-drop networks.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: A parity bit in serial communication provides:
explanation: It cannot detect an even number of bit errors and cannot correct anything.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: A framing error in a UART indicates that:
options: The stop bit was not detected at the expected time
explanation: It usually means a baud rate mismatch or line noise.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: Hardware flow control in RS232 uses which signal pair?
explanation: XON/XOFF characters provide the software alternative to hardware handshaking.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: USB compared with RS232 offers:
options: Higher speed, hot plugging and bus-supplied power
explanation: USB uses differential NRZI signalling on a host-controlled polled bus.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: The SPI bus uses which set of signal lines?
options: MOSI, MISO, SCLK and a slave select line per device
explanation: It is a full-duplex synchronous master-slave interface.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: The I2C bus uses:
options: Two wires, SDA and SCL, both open-drain with pull-ups
explanation: Multiple masters and slaves share the same two-wire bus.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: Devices on an I2C bus are distinguished by:
options: A 7-bit (or 10-bit) address transmitted after the start condition
A separate chip select pin each
explanation: The eighth bit of the address byte indicates a read or write operation.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: A major advantage of SPI over I2C is:
options: Much higher data rate and full-duplex operation
explanation: SPI trades pin count for speed; I2C trades speed for wiring simplicity.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: An I2C START condition is defined as:
options: A high-to-low transition of SDA while SCL is high
A low-to-high transition of SDA while SCL is high
explanation: STOP is the reverse: SDA going low to high while SCL is high.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: Acknowledgement in I2C is signalled by the receiver:
options: Pulling SDA low during the ninth clock pulse
explanation: A NACK (SDA left high) terminates the transfer or indicates the last byte.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: Standard mode I2C operates at a maximum clock rate of:
explanation: Fast mode is 400 kHz, fast mode plus 1 MHz and high speed mode 3.4 MHz.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: Clock stretching in I2C allows:
options: A slow slave to hold SCL low until it is ready
Two masters to transmit at once
explanation: It provides simple flow control without extra signal lines.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: Multi-master arbitration in I2C is resolved by:
options: Wired-AND behaviour, where the master writing a 1 but reading a 0 loses
explanation: Arbitration is non-destructive; the winning master's message continues uninterrupted.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: SPI clock polarity (CPOL) and phase (CPHA) together define:
options: Four possible SPI modes determining the sampling edge
explanation: Master and slave must be configured for the same mode to communicate correctly.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: A disadvantage of SPI in a system with many peripherals is:
options: One dedicated slave-select line is needed per device
explanation: Pin count grows linearly with the number of slaves, unlike I2C addressing.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Wireless protocols: Bluetooth and Zigbee
stem: Bluetooth operates in which frequency band?
explanation: It uses frequency-hopping spread spectrum over 79 channels of 1 MHz each.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Wireless protocols: Bluetooth and Zigbee
stem: A Bluetooth piconet consists of:
options: One master and up to seven active slave devices
explanation: Interconnected piconets form a scatternet.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Wireless protocols: Bluetooth and Zigbee
stem: Bluetooth uses which multiple access technique to avoid interference?
explanation: It hops 1600 times per second, greatly reducing narrowband interference.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Wireless protocols: Bluetooth and Zigbee
stem: Zigbee is based on which IEEE standard?
explanation: Bluetooth is 802.15.1, Wi-Fi is 802.11 and Ethernet is 802.3.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Wireless protocols: Bluetooth and Zigbee
stem: Zigbee is preferred over Bluetooth for sensor networks because it offers:
options: Very low power consumption, mesh networking and support for many nodes
explanation: Its 250 kbps rate is low but nodes can run for years on a battery.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Wireless protocols: Bluetooth and Zigbee
stem: The maximum data rate of Zigbee in the 2.4 GHz band is:
explanation: Lower rates of 20 and 40 kbps apply in the 868 and 915 MHz bands.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Wireless protocols: Bluetooth and Zigbee
stem: Zigbee network topologies include:
explanation: Mesh routing provides self-healing multi-hop paths between nodes.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Wireless protocols: Bluetooth and Zigbee
stem: A Zigbee coordinator differs from a router or end device in that it:
options: Forms the network and holds the overall network information
explanation: Only end devices may sleep; coordinators and routers must stay awake.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Wireless protocols: Bluetooth and Zigbee
stem: A Bluetooth module such as the HC-05 connects to a microcontroller through:
options: A UART serial interface using TXD and RXD
explanation: It behaves as a transparent wireless replacement for a serial cable.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Wireless protocols: Bluetooth and Zigbee
stem: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) was introduced primarily to:
options: Reduce power consumption for periodic small data transfers
explanation: It is widely used in wearables and IoT sensor beacons.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem: In the 8051, the SCON register is used to:
options: Configure the serial port mode and hold the RI and TI flags
explanation: Serial mode 1 with Timer 1 in auto-reload is the standard UART configuration.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: I2C requires a separate chip select line for each slave device.
explanation: Slaves are selected by address on the shared two-wire bus; SPI is the one needing select lines.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Wireless protocols: Bluetooth and Zigbee
stem: Zigbee supports mesh networking with self-healing routes.
explanation: Multi-hop mesh routing allows nodes to find alternative paths if a link fails.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem:
Assertion (A): I2C lines must be terminated with pull-up resistors.
Reason (R): SDA and SCL are driven by open-drain output stages.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Open-drain drivers can only pull low, so external pull-ups supply the logic high level.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Synchronous and asynchronous serial communication, RS232
stem:
Assertion (A): RS232 is unsuitable for long-distance industrial communication.
Reason (R): It uses single-ended signalling referenced to a common ground.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Ground offsets and noise limit it to about 15 m, so differential RS485 is used instead.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: SPI and I2C serial buses
stem: Which statements comparing SPI and I2C are correct?
options: SPI is full duplex while I2C is half duplex
explanation: SPI has no addressing scheme; it selects devices with dedicated chip select lines.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessor and Microcontroller, Unit 4

topic: Course overview: assembly language programming ability
stem: Assembly language is best described as:
options: A low level language using mnemonics that map one to one onto machine instructions
explanation: Each mnemonic corresponds directly to one machine opcode.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Course overview: assembly language programming ability
stem: The program that converts assembly source code into machine code is called:
explanation: A compiler performs the same job for high level languages.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Course overview: assembly language programming ability
stem: The main advantage of assembly language over C for microcontroller work is:
options: Precise control of timing, registers and code size
explanation: Its drawback is poor portability and much longer development time.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Course overview: assembly language programming ability
stem: A cross assembler is one that:
options: Runs on one machine but produces code for a different target processor
explanation: Embedded development almost always uses cross tools on a PC host.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Course overview: assembly language programming ability
stem: A directive such as ORG or EQU in an assembly program is:
options: An instruction to the assembler that generates no machine code
explanation: Directives control location counters, symbols and data allocation.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Course overview: assembly language programming ability
stem: A label in an assembly language program represents:
options: A symbolic address that the assembler resolves to a memory location
explanation: Labels make branch and call targets readable and relocatable.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Course overview: assembly language programming ability
stem: A two pass assembler needs two passes primarily to:
options: Resolve forward references to labels defined later in the source
explanation: Pass one builds the symbol table and pass two generates the code.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Interfacing design of peripherals: I/O, ADC, DAC, timers
stem: An ADC is used in a microcontroller system to:
options: Convert an analogue sensor signal into a digital value the CPU can process
explanation: Typical resolutions are 8, 10 or 12 bits.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Interfacing design of peripherals: I/O, ADC, DAC, timers
stem: A DAC in an embedded system is used to:
options: Produce an analogue output voltage from a digital code
explanation: It is used for waveform generation and analogue control signals.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Interfacing design of peripherals: I/O, ADC, DAC, timers
stem: A timer peripheral in a microcontroller can be used for:
options: Generating accurate delays, measuring intervals and producing PWM
explanation: It counts clock pulses independently of the CPU.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Interfacing design of peripherals: I/O, ADC, DAC, timers
stem: When a timer is configured as a counter, it counts:
options: External events applied to a dedicated input pin
explanation: A timer counts internal machine cycles; a counter counts external transitions.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Interfacing design of peripherals: I/O, ADC, DAC, timers
stem: Memory mapped I/O means that:
options: I/O has a separate address space
I/O ports share the same address space as memory and use normal memory instructions
explanation: Isolated I/O instead uses dedicated IN and OUT instructions.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Interfacing design of peripherals: I/O, ADC, DAC, timers
stem: Polling as an I/O technique means the CPU:
options: Repeatedly checks a device status flag, wasting processor time
explanation: Interrupt driven I/O frees the CPU for other work.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Interfacing design of peripherals: I/O, ADC, DAC, timers
stem: An interrupt is preferred over polling because it:
options: Lets the CPU respond to an event only when it occurs
explanation: This greatly improves CPU utilisation in real time systems.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Interfacing design of peripherals: I/O, ADC, DAC, timers
stem: A latch or buffer is used in I/O interfacing to:
options: Hold output data stable and provide drive capability to the peripheral
explanation: The 74LS373 and 74LS244 are classic examples.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Interfacing design of peripherals: I/O, ADC, DAC, timers
stem: Address decoding logic in a microcontroller system is required to:
options: Generate individual chip select signals for each memory or I/O device
explanation: Partial decoding saves gates but creates image or foldback addresses.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: The essential difference between a microprocessor and a microcontroller is that a microcontroller:
options: Integrates CPU, memory and peripherals on a single chip
explanation: A microprocessor needs external memory and I/O devices.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: An embedded system is defined as:
options: A computing system dedicated to a specific function within a larger product
explanation: It typically has real time constraints and limited resources.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: Typical characteristics of an embedded system include:
options: Dedicated function, real time operation, low cost and limited resources
explanation: Reliability and low power consumption are also key requirements.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: A hard real time system is one in which:
options: Missing a deadline constitutes a total system failure
explanation: Airbag controllers and flight control systems are hard real time.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: The role of a microcontroller in an embedded system is to:
options: Provide a graphical user interface only
Read sensors, execute control logic and drive actuators
explanation: It is the intelligence at the heart of the product.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: A watchdog timer in a microcontroller is used to:
options: Reset the system if the software fails to refresh it within a set time
explanation: It recovers the system from software lockups or noise induced faults.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: An RTOS is used in an embedded design to:
options: Schedule multiple tasks with deterministic timing behaviour
explanation: FreeRTOS and uC/OS are common small footprint examples.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: The firmware of an embedded system is normally stored in:
explanation: RAM holds only variables and the stack during execution.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: In-system programming (ISP) allows a microcontroller to be:
options: Programmed while soldered in the target circuit, usually over SPI or JTAG
explanation: It greatly simplifies field firmware updates.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: A bootloader in a microcontroller is a small program that:
options: Resides in protected memory and loads new application firmware
explanation: It allows updates through UART, USB or a network without a programmer.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Course overview: assembly language programming ability
stem: A simulator differs from an emulator in that a simulator:
options: Models the processor in software without any target hardware
explanation: An in-circuit emulator gives real time debugging on the actual hardware.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Course overview: assembly language programming ability
stem: A breakpoint in a debugging tool is used to:
options: Halt execution at a chosen instruction so registers and memory can be inspected
explanation: Single stepping then allows instruction by instruction examination.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: Compared with an 8-bit microcontroller, a 32-bit device typically offers:
options: Higher throughput, larger address space and richer peripherals
explanation: 8-bit parts still dominate cost sensitive, simple applications.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Interfacing design of peripherals: I/O, ADC, DAC, timers
stem: DMA (direct memory access) improves system performance by:
options: Transferring data between memory and a peripheral without CPU intervention
explanation: The CPU is only interrupted when the whole block transfer completes.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Developing systems using different microcontrollers
stem: A microcontroller contains CPU, memory and I/O peripherals on one chip.
explanation: This single chip integration is what distinguishes it from a microprocessor.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Course overview: assembly language programming ability
stem: Assembly language programs are highly portable between different processor families.
explanation: Each instruction set is unique, so assembly must be rewritten for a new architecture.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1

topic: Interfacing design of peripherals: I/O, ADC, DAC, timers
stem:
Assertion (A): Interrupt driven I/O is more efficient than polling.
Reason (R): In interrupt driven I/O the CPU is notified by hardware only when the device needs service.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Polling wastes processor cycles continuously testing a status flag.
source: BEU syllabus — Microprocessors, Unit 1
